title: Surge buffering and regional SKU carveout simulation
content:
Purpose
Quick simulator sheet for planning a regional surge buffer + SKU carveout approach for hosted API. Goal: (1) size transient reserve pools per region, (2) identify candidate SKU splits for latency-aware pricing, (3) estimate marginal COGS impact during 2x and 5x surge, and (4) summarize operational tradeoffs. Working draft — numbers are illustrative.

Summary assumptions (global)
- Base price assumptions: retail price expressed as $ per 1M tokens equivalent (for simple margin calc).
- Time horizon: short-run (monthly amortization buckets) for reserve sizing.
- Surge definition: 2x = sustained 2x baseline for 30m-2h; 5x = sustained for 10-60m.
- Buffering strategy: combination of reserved capacity (dedicated slots), spot-style burst, and model fallbacks.
- Currency: USD. GPU+infra COGS include amortized GPU (license + infra), power, rack, network egress estimate.

Key parameters (editable)
- Baseline utilization: 60% on reserved pools in NA, 55% EU, 40% APAC
- Baseline per-region average sequence length: NA=110 tokens, EU=95, APAC=80
- Baseline request mix: 50% chat-gen (large), 30% completion (medium), 20% embedding-ish (small)
- Model families: alpha-large (L), bravo-medium (M), charlie-small (S)

Main table (sample rows)
Region | Model | Base PPK ($/1M tokens) | GPU amort ($/1M) | Network+IO ($/1M) | Ops overhead ($/1M) | Base COGS ($/1M) | Retail price ($/1M) | Gross margin (%) | Surge factor | COGS @ 2x surge ($/1M) | COGS @ 5x surge ($/1M) | Recommended buffer pool (vGPU-equivalents) | Note
NA | alpha-L | 110.0 | 58.0 | 8.0 | 6.0 | 72.0 | 160.0 | 55.0 | 2x | 84.0 | 96.5 | 48 | latency-sensitive, keep reserve
EU | alpha-L | 115.0 | 60.5 | 9.0 | 6.5 | 76.0 | 175.0 | 56.6 | 2x | 89.5 | 103.0 | 24 | higher network -> higher surge premium
APAC | bravo-M | 45.0 | 22.0 | 6.0 | 4.0 | 32.0 | 75.0 | 57.3 | 2x | 38.5 | 45.0 | 12 | lower base sequence lengths
NA | charlie-S | 12.0 | 4.5 | 2.5 | 1.2 | 8.2 | 20.0 | 59.0 | 2x | 9.0 | 10.2 | 8 | batch-friendly

Notes on table numbers: COGS @ 2x surge assumes reduced amortization dilution (i.e., reserved capacity is consumed faster) plus ~10% extra ops overhead from queueing and retries. COGS @ 5x surge includes additional tail inefficiencies and 15% premium for spot/overflow egress and preemptions. Columns are editable cells in sheet.

Surge buffer sizing logic (simple heuristics)
1) Desired SLO coverage: we want to avoid caller-visible tail latency for 99% of requests during a 2x event for <=1hr.
2) Reserve sizing formula (rough): reserve_vGPUs = ceil((peak_tokens_per_minute * average_kv_per_token) / tokens_per_vGPU_per_minute) * safety_factor. For rough sizing we use safety_factor=1.15 for regional warm pools.
3) For our sample NA alpha-L waveform: baseline slot need = 40 vGPUs equivalent. To cover 2x surge for 1h plus warmup: add 48 (20% extra) -> matches table.

SKU carveout proposal (high-level)
- SKU A (latency-priority): pinned reserved capacity, higher price, lower batching, strict SLOs. Target customers: platform SDK where interactive latency matters.
- SKU B (balanced): mixed reserved + burstable, medium price, batching encouraged. Target: general API usage.
- SKU C (economy/batch): fully batch-optimized, aggressive quantization, cheaper fallback models, lower price. Target: high-throughput low-latency-constraint workloads.

Pricing and margin levers (simulated)
- Add latency surcharge: +10-35% price uplift for SKU A depending on region and model family.
- Buffer amortization allocation: spread reserve pool cost over SKU A only (if small set of tenants use it) vs across all SKUs (if many use it). Example: NA reserved pool (48 vGPUs) amortized -> ~$X/month -> if allocated to 5 tenants increases their PPK by ~3-6% each.
- Fallback effectiveness: estimate percentage of requests served by cheaper fallback during surge. E.g., 20% fallback reduces surge COGS by ~8-12% depending on mix.

Simulated scenario outputs (quick picks)
- Scenario 1: 2x surge, no fallback, shared reserve spread: NA marginal PPK increases by ~14% for alpha-L; retail margin drops from 55% to 46% short-run.
- Scenario 2: 2x surge, 20% fallback to bravo-M, reserved pool dedicated to latency customers: margin for latency SKU preserved (~52%), general SKU margin drops more.
- Scenario 3: 5x short spike, aggressive fallback + spot burst: operational risk high (preemptions), expected temporary visible degradation; margin hit up to 25% for general requests.

Operational recommendations (priority ordered)
1) Create a small dedicated reserve pool in NA and EU for latency-priority SKU sized for 2x 1hr events (NA ~48 vGPUs, EU ~24 vGPUs) and pilot for 6 weeks.
2) Introduce explicit SKU split with documented SLOs and a latency surcharge; start with +15% uplift for SKU A in NA, +20% in EU (higher egress).
3) Implement model fallback path: alpha-L -> bravo-M with graceful decoding truncation; instrument fallback ratio and quality delta with eval prompts.
4) Build a quick dashboard surfaced in Console showing: real-time reserve utilization, fallback ratio, marginal PPK during surges, and projected margin impact.
5) Test spot-burst option with kill/rollback policy in a staging region to measure preemption rates and cost deltas.

Short TODOs and open questions
- TODO: compute amortized $/month per vGPU for dedicated stride (Diego).
- TODO: run Monte Carlo on request shape (Priya) to estimate probability mass above 2x for NA and EU.
- Open: how to bill customers who opt into SKU A but don't consume reserve pool (empty slot allocation policy). Confluence thread proposed.
- Open: legal/contract implications for SLA tiers and credits for surge-induced latencies. Ops/legal sync required.

Appendix: quick sensitivity checks (hand calc style)
- If fallback is 30% effective during surge and fallback PPK is 60% of primary, effective COGS up to 2x = base*0.7 + fallback*0.3 -> net % improvement ~9-14% depending on region.
- If reserved pool amortization is reallocated across all tokens rather than SKU-limited, per-token amort increases by ~0.6% but spreads risk.

Contact and provenance
Sheet owner: Maya Chen (product-optimize); initial draft based on internal infra cost snapshots (Nov 2025) and previous optimize playbooks. See linked artifacts for simulation notebooks and JIRA tasks.

Notes-to-self: keep numbers coarse for initial sync with GTM; we will iterate after Monte Carlo from Priya.
